dct_description_sm:
Baseball backstops: Backstops protect spectators and keep the ball in the field of play.  They vary in size and style.  Construction material consists of galvanized pipe and mesh.  Some have nylon protective netting on top.  Some may have wooden baseboards and/or concrete retaining walls.

Baseball bases, plates, and anchors: home plate, pitcher's rubber, base anchors.  Installed seasonally.  Base anchors are constructed of steel inserted into a concrete base, home plate and pitchers plate is constructed of a wood base with rubber on top.

Basketball hoops and nets: post, backboard, hoop and net provided for play.  Backboards are either fixed or adjustable and made from either fibreglass, wood, metal or plexiglass.

Cricket poles and net: wooden poles supporting nylon protective netting.  Posts are engineered.

Rugby posts: Removable powder-coated aluminum uprights provided seasonally, hinged on concrete footings.

Soccer goals: Portable aluminum goalposts provided seasonally; three different sizes.  Nylon mesh netting supplied at two locations.

Tennis net and post: metal uprights to support nylon net, most with adjustable turnbuckles.

Volleyball pole: galvanized metal pole.

Water Park Equipment: A user activated water play feature comprised of 4 nozzles set in the concrete surface at grade which sprays water into the air.  Seasonally available.  Water is not recycled.  Falls under Island Health regulations.

Watering Can: Stainless steel stucture in the shape of a watering can with various jets and nozzles providing differing patterns of water flow. A single push of a button will cause several valves to open in sequence.  Seasonally available.  Controller is computer based.  Surface is concrete.  Falls under Island Health regulations.

Data are updated by city staff as needed, and automatically copied to the Open Data Portal. The "Last Updated" date shown on our Open Data Portal refers to the last time the data schema was modified in the portal, or any changes were made to this description.  We update our data through automated scripts which does not trigger the "last updated" date to change.

Note: Attributes represent each field in a dataset, and some fields will contain information such as ID numbers.  As a result some visualizations on the tabs on our Open Data page will not be relevant.
